html:
The Kashmir earthquake struck on the morning of 8 October 2005, centred near Muzaffarabad in Pakistani Azad Kashmir. It measured 7.6 and killed about 87,000 people, almost all in Pakistan, with about 1,300 more in Indian Kashmir.

It hit on a Saturday morning, a school day, and thousands of children died when badly built schools fell. Whole towns such as Balakot in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were ruined, and landslides cut mountain roads, so help was slow to reach many valleys before winter.

The disaster brought a rare moment of cooperation across the Line of Control that divides Kashmir. India sent aid, and the two countries opened crossing points so that families could meet and relief could pass. Pakistan's government under Pervez Musharraf ran a large rebuilding effort with foreign money, and new building codes followed. Four years earlier, the Gujarat earthquake had shown how deadly weak buildings are in South Asian quakes.
